how then be i mad
hearken
and observe how healthily how calmly i can tell you the whole story

object there be none
passion there be none
i love the old man
he have never wrong i
he have never give i insult
for his gold i have no desire
i think it be his eye
yes it be this
one of his eye resemble that of a vulture a pale blue eye with a film over it
whenever it fall upon i my blood run cold and so by degree very gradually i make up my mind to take the life of the old man and thus rid myself of the eye for ever
now this be the point
you fancy i mad
madman know nothing
but you should have see i
you should have see how wisely i proceed with what caution with what foresight with what dissimulation i go to work
i be never kind to the old man than during the whole week before i kill he
and every night about midnight i turn the latch of his door and open it oh so gently
and then when i have make an opening sufficient for my head i put in a dark lantern all close closed so that no light shine out and then i thrust in my head
oh you would have laugh to see how cunningly i thrust it in
i move it slowly very very slowly so that i might not disturb the old man ’s sleep
it take i an hour to place my whole head within the opening so far that i could see he as he lie upon the tell tale heart 4 his bed
ha!—would a madman have be so wise as this
and then when my head be well in the room i undo the lantern cautiously oh so cautiously cautiously for the hinge creaked)—i undo it just so much that a single thin ray fall upon the vulture eye
and this i do for seven long night every night just at midnight but i find the eye always close
and so it be impossible to do the work for it be not the old man who vex i but his evil eye
and every morning when the day break i go boldly into the chamber and speak courageously to he call he by name in a hearty tone and inquire how he have pass the night
so you see he would have be a very profound old man indeed to suspect that every night just at twelve i look in upon he while he sleep
upon the eighth night i be more than usually cautious in open the door
a watch ’s minute hand move more quickly than do mine
never before that night have i feel the extent of my own power of my sagacity
i could scarcely contain my feeling of triumph
to think that there i be open the door little by little and he not even to dream of my secret deed or thought
i fairly chuckle at the idea and perhaps he hear i for he move on the bed suddenly as if startle
now you may think that i draw back but no

his room be as black as pitch with the thick darkness for the shutter be close fasten through fear of robber and so i know that he could not see the opening of the door and i keep push it on steadily steadily
i have my head in and be about to open the lantern when my thumb slip upon the tin fastening and the old man spring up in the bed cry out—“who ’s there
i keep quite still and say nothing
for a whole hour i do not move a muscle and in the meantime i do not hear he lie down
